tabs.label: Am Telefon
tabs.instructions: In a German-speaking office, people answer the phone with the department and their surname. Listen, then open the transcript.

transcript: Frau Schneider: Sekretariat, Schneider, guten Tag. Office, Schneider speaking. Hello.
Lukas: Guten Tag, Frau Schneider. Hier ist Lukas Neumann. Ist Frau Keller da? Hello, Ms Schneider. This is Lukas Neumann. Is Ms Keller there?
Frau Schneider: Einen Moment, bitte. Frau Keller, Telefon für Sie! One moment, please. Ms Keller, telephone for you!
Lukas: Guten Tag, Frau Keller. Hier ist Lukas Neumann. Hello, Ms Keller. This is Lukas Neumann.

text:
• Sekretariat, Schneider, guten Tag. – answering with department and surname
  • Hier ist … – This is … (when you call)
  • Ist Frau … da? – Is Ms … there?
  • Einen Moment, bitte. – One moment, please.

tabs.label: Notes
tabs.instructions: Two things English speakers often miss.
text: Do not say “Hello, it’s me” to someone you do not know well. Give your full name: Hier ist Lukas Neumann.
An office or business phone is answered with Sie and the name of the office or the surname. At home people often say Hallo or just their name.
